title: Eval alerting playbook & regression test additions after prod-quality incident
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Production anomaly on 2026-02-18 where a model/config rollout produced a 4-point drop in our QA metric for the conversational completion task (observed only by customer reports and sparse eval coverage). This ticket tracks the postmortem follow-up work: close eval gaps exposed by the incident, add smoke/canary evals that run on config and model changes, and codify an alerting + remediation playbook that ties eval deltas to rollout automation (pauses/rollbacks).

Problem statement: Our current eval surface lacks deterministic coverage for the specific prompt families that regressed and does not automatically block or pause rollouts when quality deltas exceed thresholds. The incident surfaced three gaps: 1) missing targeted evals for customer prompt clusters, 2) no per-change canary smoke eval step in CI/CD, 3) lack of an automated threshold-based rollback hook in rollout controller.

Objective: Deliver a minimal but high-value set of tests, monitoring and playbook items so future incidents are detected before customer impact and can be mitigated automatically or quickly rolled back. Focus is on cost-effective eval placement (canary + daily heavy suite) and clear ownerable runbooks for ops and SRE.
acceptance_criteria: Create 6 targeted evals that reproduce the prod regressions for top-3 customer prompt clusters and add them to the golden-suite
Add a lightweight canary smoke job that runs on any model/config change and fails the rollout if QA-score delta >= 2 points on any targeted eval
Wire canary job into GitHub Actions + Redwood rollout controller so failing canary pauses canary/rollout and notifies on-call
Add dashboard card in Console showing eval deltas (7-day baseline vs canary) with links to failing examples
Document playbook in Confluence with step-by-step rollback and postmortem checklist
tasks: T1: Reconstruct failure traces and collect 200 representative prompts from incident (Maya)
T2: Implement 6 targeted eval scenarios in evals repo and add expected annotations (Ethan)
T3: Add smoke/canary job in CI pipeline that runs 1-minute cost-limited checks (ENG infra)
T4: Extend rollout controller to accept 'evalGate' config and fail fast on threshold breaches (Core runtime)
T5: Create Console dashboard card + link to failing examples (Observability)
T6: Draft and review playbook doc; run tabletop exercise with SRE and PM (Maya, Diego)
T7: Backfill evaluations on last 30 days of rollouts to find any silent regressions (Data team)
T8: Add integration test that validates canary job triggers on model-version bump (CI)
T9: Close follow-up PRs and merge to main; monitor 72h after deployment

2026-02-25 - Riley (SRE): Agreed to add an on-call notification path; suggested adding metrics for 'fraction of failing evals' as a signal. Concern about churn if thresholds too tight.
2026-03-01 - PM Diego Ramos: Prioritized 6 targeted evals; asked to make canary smoke job under 5 minutes and cost < $1 per run. Approved by product leadership for runtime-1.21 milestone.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Anika Gupta): Suggested UX for Console card showing before/after diff and example counterfactuals; added guidance to link to PR and failing examples.

2026-03-09 - Ethan Liu: Implemented canonical evals and submitted PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/341. Running nightly backfill; 14 historical rollouts flagged, 2 with minor regressions.

2026-03-11 - Maya Patel: Wire-up to rollout controller PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-controller/pull/127. Manual canary run paused as expected on simulated failure. Next: refine alert thresholds and add hysteresis to avoid flapping.
resolution: Triage complete. Work in progress to add targeted evals, canary gate and dashboard. Manual mitigations used during incident; automation will reduce future MTTR and customer exposure.
